dataset_family: ADNI (ADNI-GO and ADNI-2 phases; public multi-site North American cohort)
method_family: Structural MRI morphometry (FreeSurfer cortical features, Brainnetome nuclear volumes) with mRMR/LASSO scores, causal structure discovery (GES) and a logistic-regression nomogram. The GDS evidence itself is a univariate baseline comparison of converters versus stable MCI (t-test or Mann-Whitney), the same kind of analysis as P-647's Table 4 GDS comparison.
what_it_shows: The sample is 162 ADNI MCI patients followed for five years: 68 progressed to AD and 94 stayed stable. Baseline GDS was 1.96 (SD 1.62) in progressors and 1.71 (SD 1.57) in stable patients, p = 0.339. GDS is reported only as a baseline characteristic. It was not entered into the causal graph, the prediction models or the nomogram, and the paper reports no GDS-MRI analysis.
why: PARTLY. The study shows one element of the row's severity clause: a continuous baseline depression score (GDS) did not separate five-year converters from non-converters. It does not test the first clause, because every participant has MCI and there is no non-MCI or non-depressed comparator. It also has MRI but never relates GDS to any brain measure. LIMITS: (1) This is an incidental Table 1 baseline comparison, not a planned or adjusted test. (2) The GDS range is narrow and low (overall mean 1.81, SD 1.59), so a null result is expected from range restriction. The PDF does not state ADNI's depression entry criterion, so the cap the finder mentions cannot be confirmed from this document, although the printed distribution is consistent with such a cap. (3) The 162 patients were selected under 'stringent inclusion criteria', and the authors list the small sample as a limitation. CORRECTION TO THE FINDER NOTES: the block says no GDS values are printed, but Table 1 of the PDF prints them. INDEPENDENCE: no current supporter uses ADNI (their datasets are Korea University Guro, the Shanghai Brain Health Cohort, Shanghai Tongji and Florence). No authors are shared with the supporters or with the other candidates. ADNI is, however, the dataset family of P-26, which the row cites outside the supporter list with the opposite result for the 36-month trajectory. If P-26 were ever counted, only one of the two could count. METHOD: the relevant test is the same univariate converter-versus-stable baseline comparison that carries P-647's conversion result, so on the method-family rule it adds little distinct method evidence for that limb.
